records.title: Shannon information theory and channel coding as a quantitative communication framework
records.sourceNativeSummary: Shannon’s 1948 framework separated message meaning from the engineering problem of transmitting symbols through noisy channels, quantified information, and established capacity/error-control limits that later coding systems could approach.
records.rivalOrBoundary: A mathematical capacity theorem did not itself supply practical codes, hardware or latency/cost tradeoffs; Hamming and later coding work were required to turn limits into usable systems.

sources.supports: Shannon 1948 information/channel-capacity foundation and coding implication
information theory, entropy/channel capacity and implementation-independent limits

records.title: Linear programming and simplex optimization in postwar operations research
records.sourceNativeSummary: Dantzig’s simplex method made large classes of linear allocation problems computationally tractable enough for postwar military and industrial planning; OR institutions then diffused these formal decision tools.
records.rivalOrBoundary: An optimizer returns the optimum of the modeled objective/constraints, not the optimum of reality; missing nonlinearities, uncertain data and political objectives remain outside the solved linear program.

sources.supports: simplex method and linear programming history
Dantzig oral history and OR context

records.title: Kalman filtering as model-based dynamic estimation
records.sourceNativeSummary: Kalman-style recursive state estimation allowed noisy sequential measurements and a dynamical model to be combined into continuously updated position/velocity estimates; NASA adopted variants for spaceflight navigation under tight computing constraints.
records.rivalOrBoundary: Filter quality depends on model/noise assumptions and initialization; a compact state estimate is not the underlying physical state and can be confidently wrong under model mismatch.

sources.supports: Kalman/Schmidt development and Apollo navigation constraints
1965 Kalman-Schmidt filter explanation for space navigation

records.title: Magnetic-core memory as reliable random-access computing infrastructure
records.sourceNativeSummary: MIT Whirlwind work replaced fragile electrostatic storage with coincident-current ferrite core memory; manufacturing improvements reduced assembly time and core memory became the dominant random-access memory for roughly the mid-1950s through early 1970s.
records.rivalOrBoundary: Memory success depended on labor-intensive core-plane manufacture and system integration; it was later displaced by semiconductor memory despite being a durable platform for its regime.

sources.supports: Whirlwind core-memory motivation, development, assembly and diffusion
IBM 702 transition from CRT memory to magnetic core in 1956

records.title: ARPANET first-node deployment after packet-network research
records.sourceNativeSummary: ARPA contracted BBN in 1968 for IMPs and activated the initial four-node ARPANET in 1969, turning heterogeneous-computer resource-sharing/network research into a working packet network.
records.rivalOrBoundary: Four operational nodes proved a network substrate, not the later Internet; interoperability protocols, scaling, radio/satellite internetworking and governance remained future frontiers.

sources.supports: four nodes, 1969 first signal, IMPs and packet-network problem

records.title: Glaser bubble chamber opening high-energy particle observation
records.sourceNativeSummary: Glaser’s bubble chamber turned charged-particle tracks into visible/photographable evidence, and larger chambers became key instruments for high-energy particle discoveries.
records.rivalOrBoundary: The instrument expanded observation capacity but interpretation still depended on beam conditions, reconstruction, theory and large human/data-analysis workflows.

sources.supports: bubble chamber invention and particle-physics measurement role

records.title: Nuclear magnetic resonance as a new molecular and precision measurement method
records.sourceNativeSummary: Bloch and Purcell independently developed nuclear magnetic resonance methods in 1946, enabling precision measurement of nuclear magnetic properties and later molecular/material analysis.
records.rivalOrBoundary: A sensitive resonance phenomenon is not automatically a universal imaging/spectroscopy platform; magnets, pulse/control methods, signal processing and domain-specific interpretation developed later.

sources.supports: Bloch/Purcell nuclear magnetic precision measurement award and method
